correctness.rationale: The exact local formula follows by partitioning zero-, one-, and two-position substitutions; adjacent changes require excluding q-d_i equal replacements while nonadjacent changes multiply. Writing b=q-3 and e_i for distance-two equality, internal four-letter distinctness h_i satisfies 1-e_i e_{i+1} <= h_i <= 2-e_i-e_{i+1}. Lower-bound difference is at least E+2M-A+b(n-3)E plus nonnegative terms, with A<=E-1 for E>0; equality forces a three-periodic proper word. The upper-bound difference is at least (q-2)sum k_i z_i - sum z_i; for q=3 the remaining endpoint-defect case has a strict loss through a nonadjacent interior pair at n>=5. Thus the claimed formulas and exactly counted equality cases hold for all q>=3,n>=5. A separately written enumerator checked 65,376 finite centers (q=3..6) against local formula and stated sharp cases; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

Their construction tables and algorithm do not count allowable radius-two substitution neighbors around each homopolymer-free source; lower bounds on codebook cardinality do not imply sphere sizes. originality.rationale: Examined arXiv:2405.20368 (introduction, technical regime sections, conclusion) and DOI:10.3389/fgene.2023.1158337 (constraints, algorithm, tables, conclusion) and compared theorem-level implications. Actual targeted searches of public literature and a mathematical-finding index returned related unconstrained Hamming volumes, radius-two Turan-mass studies, proper-coloring noise codebooks, and graph-coloring packing, but no result asserting the all-q,n center formula with sharp period-two and period-three extremizers. An earlier exact local-sphere theorem might be indexed under graph coloring reconfiguration, proper-word substitution neighborhoods, or a different sphere/metric name.
Search does not certify absence from every journal, thesis or unindexed table.

value.rationale: The exact center-dependent error-neighborhood volume for a homopolymer-free language is an information-theoretically motivated metric invariant, needed to quantify finite-block packing and reconstruction geometry. Sharp lower and upper volumes, rigid period-three and period-two equality cases, and a q=3 change from linear to quadratic volume spread are structural facts, not mere renamings of unrestricted Hamming balls or isolated small-length computations. The result is a complete all-length extremal classification with an explicit finite-radius proof; it does not claim optimal code size.
